summary: Phase 9 iteration 7: 6/6 backend tests pass and full frontend flow green (0 console errors on /dashboard + /admin). CRITICAL bug found & fixed in /api/knowledge/crawl: NameError 'prod_urls is not defined' at server.py:532 (500 on every crawl). Applied minimal fix: build imgs[] + prod_urls[] from anchor+img pairs so every catalog item now includes a 'url' field. Verified: crawl returns 4 Apple items each with 'url' key. Known limitation retained: apple.com/shop/buy-iphone is JS-heavy so static requests.get finds no product anchors, and all 4 urls fall back to the crawled URL (documented in test). [[LANG:xx]] marker verified at very start of every chat reply. [[BUY:name|url]] marker verified when visitor expresses buying intent ('I want to buy the iPhone. Add it to my cart.'). Voice-only fullscreen overlay: startcall → overlay appears (with .voice-halo + .face-alive/.face-speaking inside), endcall-fullscreen dismisses it. Preview modal now renders the Widget inside (360x423, product cards + avatar visible). Avatar PNGs still ~2MB from OpenAI gpt-image-1. One minor miss reported: main idle does NOT carry class 'face-alive' (only the voice-overlay avatar container does); animated breathing/sway isn't applied to the main widget avatar image.

minor.issue: Static requests.get crawler cannot resolve JS-rendered product anchors (apple.com), so all extracted items get the same fallback URL. Consider Playwright/browserless for JS-heavy shops.

ui_bugs.issue: class 'face-alive' is NOT applied to the idle main avatar image (data-testid=widget-avatar-image). It only lives inside the voice-only-overlay avatar container. Continuous breathing/sway/blink animation therefore does not run on the primary embedded widget avatar as described in Phase 9 feature (1).

rca of the issue: server.py /api/knowledge/crawl referenced `prod_urls` list at line 532 but the previous implementation only built an `imgs` list. As delivered by main agent, every crawl POST returned 500 NameError. Reproduction: `curl -X POST /api/knowledge/crawl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <demo-token>' -d '{"url":"https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-iphone"}'` → HTTP 500 with backend traceback `NameError: name 'prod_urls' is not defined`. Mitigation: refactor the img loop to also capture the enclosing <a href=...> and append both to imgs[] + prod_urls[] in lockstep; when no anchor present, fallback to the crawled URL. Every catalog item now has a valid 'url' field, satisfying the Phase 9 contract for BUY-marker product links.
